gen-dafont-nordic-gf-port-lligat-slab: Ancient and blunt, with a cramped, folded look. Nordic hammers out closed, single-weight letters, while Port Lligat Slab is the one that opens up, its serif lowercase round and hugging.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-quando: Quando spreads its text serif letters wide, with a big, tall middle zone in every word. Nordic is the better heading, its strokes uniform like rod stock, while Quando handles the bookish, traditional body.
gen-dafont-nordic-outfit: Outfit reads clean and friendly, its curves stopping well short of closing. Nordic is strongest as a heading, tight and powerful with uniform strokes, while Outfit, a plain sans, does the quieter job of staying open beneath it.
gen-dafont-nordic-plus-jakarta-sans: Nordic's letters have a cramped, pressed-leaf fold and brush-dab spacing, a look that feels ancient and powerful. Big and brief is where it earns its place; Plus Jakarta Sans stays open below.
gen-dafont-nordic-sora: Ancient weight meets a modern, geometric edge. Nordic keeps its letters closed and tight, while Sora, a sans, holds its curves apart and sits at a moderate lowercase height, which is the real difference between them.
gen-dafont-nordic-space-grotesk: Space Grotesk breathes, its counters open like a hollow reed. Over a longer passage, its constant-width strokes and moderate lowercase height keep the text moving, while Nordic's taller, tighter letters stay up top.
gen-dafont-nulshock-fs-spline-sans: Technical and bold, with stretched spacing up top. Over a longer passage, Spline Sans, a sans, reads in a contemporary, friendly way, its wide curve gaps and uniform strokes keeping each line easy to follow.
gen-dafont-nulshock-fs-synonym: Stretched, bold and outlined, Nulshock looks like a machine label. Synonym, a sans-serif, sits under it as a plain stripe of ink with generous curve openings, so the loud top and the dependable body never compete.
gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-almendra: Wide, technical and outlined, with capitals barely above the lowercase. Nulshock earns its keep big and brief, while Almendra, a serif, brings a dignified, bookish feel from its deep lowercase midsection.
gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-bree-serif: Nulshock sets its stretched, outlined letters wide, with a marker-drawn plainness in every character. Big and brief is where it earns its keep, and Bree Serif, a serif, brings outsized lowercase with a literary, refined feel.
